q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a woven shirt?
title: Woven shirt carbon footprint per piece
short: Multiply the fabric issued per shirt, including cutting waste, by your mill's per-metre factor. Add interlining, buttons, thread, labels, sewing and pressing electricity, washing if any, and the folding pack. Divide by shirts passed. Fabric is usually most of the total.

ul: Fabric per shirt from the marker, including waste.
Ask the weaving or processing mill for a per-metre figure; dyeing and finishing energy is in it.
Fusible interlining, buttons, thread, labels and collar stays.
Sewing machines, fusing presses and steam irons with their boiler.
Garment washing or softening, where done.

p: Report per shirt by style, since full and half sleeves differ in fabric. Give the fabric weight in GSM.

example.title: Worked example: shirt unit per piece (one month)
lines: Steam boiler PNG: 5,000 SCM x 2.05 = 10,250 kg CO2
Plant total: 38,650 / 80,000 = 0.483 kg CO2 per shirt
Add fabric, interlining and trims for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
